source.title: Minnorm training: an algorithm for training over-parameterized deep neural networks
source.authors: Yamini Bansal; Madhu S. Advani; D. Cox; Andrew M. Saxe

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a width sweep with test generalization outcomes, using a toy regression task rather than the datasets and setup specified in V2.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports MNIST comparisons of Minnorm, SGD, and weight decay, plus toy analyses of convergence and generalization. These do not test the listed versions: they do not compare random-label and natural-label fitting, the specified CNN versus fully connected architectures, optimizer generalization, large batches, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The MNIST weight-norm bound is not the sharpness measure in V7.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 tests the width–generalization relationship in a new setting: sinusoidal regression with random, fixed first-layer weights and trained output weights. The widest network generalizes best when a low-norm interpolating solution is selected.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the tested settings. The authors propose minimum-norm constrained training for underdetermined networks with accurate labels, demonstrate favorable convergence and generalization in simplified settings, and report better MNIST test performance with no apparent overtraining.
record.recipe_differences: The width sweep is a toy regression illustration, not the specified one-hidden-layer MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 classification experiment. The real-world experiment compares a new constrained Minnorm procedure with SGD and weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Width changes the reported generalization outcome in the toy regression illustration.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, Minnorm SGD achieves 1.46 ± 0.063% test error, versus 1.82 ± 0.056% for vanilla SGD and 1.74 ± 0.051% for weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit minimum-norm constrained training can improve held-out performance over these SGD and weight-decay recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Minnorm improves a norm-based generalization bound by about fivefold and removes initialization dependence in the studied deep linear setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm training can tighten norm-based bounds and suppress harmful initialization components in underdetermined networks.

record.problems: The width sweep is a small synthetic regression illustration; the supplied text does not give a numeric test-error series or uncertainty for its width-specific outcomes. The figure's MSE values cannot be confidently assigned to individual widths from the flattened text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted. MNIST optimizer comparisons and norm-bound results were excluded because they do not measure a listed version's defining claim.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training and held-out performance.

Continued improvement across multiple widths beyond an established interpolation threshold; MNIST or CIFAR-10 classification; training all layers to convergence without explicit regularization. Figure 1 fixes random first-layer weights and explicitly selects a low-norm solution.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under matched, fixed epoch budgets. The MNIST comparisons use different learning rates and validation-selected stopping times.
Dropout effects, including interactions with training-set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the qualitative Figure 1 comparison, but not reliable assignment of its flattened MSE values. Differences from the original V2 recipe are untested extensions, not demonstrated failures of V2. Other results were explicitly declared excluded in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or random-label test accuracy comparison.
The width sweep uses a simple sinusoidal regression task with random first-layer weights and a trained second layer, not the specified MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 classification setup.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No large-batch penalty study under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with sharpness, norms, or margins as predictors of the generalization gap.
No removal of memorized training examples.
